What degraded

  • The scanner's daily ceiling could not be read. There is no Supabase connector in this environment, so scanner.scans and scanner.config were not queried and the day's scan count, the cap and any failures are unknown. A requester who hit the cap today would not have been noticed.
  • gov.texas.gov now serves User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: / and was not fetched. The registry row says it serves no robots.txt at all. Field log entry filed, registry row proposed.
  • capitol.texas.gov/TLODOCS/ is disallowed and was not fetched. The live hearing notice path is lowercase and the disallow is uppercase, and this run treated that as a disallow. /Committees/ is not disallowed and carries everything except the charge text, which lrl.texas.gov has in full.
  • aggregate_check could not re-derive a quoted figure carrying a thousands separator, because to_int did not strip the comma, so slide 4's 1,400 was declared through computed_by instead. FIXED IN THIS RUN'S UPGRADE PHASE. to_int now strips the separator before isdigit, and the self-test replays the old behaviour to prove it went red.
  • aggregate_check short-circuits a whole text node on EXEMPT, so 392 is published on slide 6 and in the caption and cannot be declared in aggregates.json. It is computed in compute.py, written to computed.json and interpolated rather than typed, and the two computation paths refuse to agree unless they match.
  • build_slides.py refused a footer collision on slide 9 and exited 1 into a suppressed stream, and the previous build's HTML was still in out/<date>/slides/, so the renderer rendered a deck that had never been built and three scoring judges graded it. Caught by a judge comparing pixels against the plan, not by any gate. Proposals 16 and 17 are the two halves of the fix.
  • sources_block.py was called with --run for the whole run and there is no --run. argparse prefix-matched --run-dir, the script took the bare date as a directory, found no printed ids, concluded every printed id resolves, and exited 0 every time it was asked. shipped_check caught the real state. Proposal 14.
  • The DPS connected and autonomous vehicles page was fetched for the absence record and not kept in the run's fetch cache, so when a scoring judge disputed the verb on slide 7 the direction could not be settled from an artifact. The frame was written to use the absence record's own words rather than to guess.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Texas authorized what was already driving, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Texas authorized what was already driving.

Aurora announced driverless freight between Dallas and Houston on May 1st, 2025. The TxDMV authorization under SB 2807 became a live requirement for commercial driverless operation on May 28th, 2026. That is 392 days later. Kodiak reported a fleet of 35 driverless trucks in the Permian Basin on June 30th, 2026. Waymo opened Houston robotaxi rides to anyone with the app on August 20th, 2026. Raul Gallegos of the National Federation for the Blind of Texas welcomed the full Houston opening.

The state Senate's transportation committee holds a public hearing August 25th, 2026 in room E1.016. One of its charges asks the committee to quantify the impact on traffic-related collisions.

That charge names three agencies whose rule making is in scope. The one that publishes the state's crash records is not among them. This record checked it anyway, and TxDOT's crash data page names no automated driving category. The per incident record this docket reached is federal.

The Legislature posts the meeting on capitol.texas.gov under Committees, Meetings Upcoming.

#SB2807 #TxDMV #PermianBasin

The machine changed itself

  • plan_render_check gains DECLARED: every display string a dossier's `type:` block declares must be on the frame that shipped
    build_slides.py refused this run's build over a slide 9 byline 72px too wide, printed the refusal to a stream the caller had suppressed, and its exit code was never read. The previous build's HTML was still in out/<date>/slides/, the renderer rendered it, every gate in the suite passed on it, and three scoring judges graded a deck that had never been built. Two repairs the run believed it had shipped existed only in storyboard.md. plan_render_check itself passed, because palettes and acceptance items are not the words. This is the tenth panel's own one sentence fix.
  • sources_block.py can no longer report clean when it was handed nothing
    it was invoked as `--run 2026-08-21` for the whole run and there is no `--run`. Argparse prefix-matched `--run-dir`, the bare date became the path, the path did not exist, no printed ids were found, every printed id therefore resolved, and it printed `sources block: clean` and exited 0 every time it was asked, including immediately after slide 6 gained two claim ids the published block did not list. shipped_check caught the real state one step later. A checker whose empty case is indistinguishable from its clean case is worse than none, because it is trusted.
  • aggregate_check.to_int reads a thousands separator, so a quoted figure at or above 1,000 can be declared through quoted_from at all
    NUM was taught to consume a thousands separator in August after '2,600 streamlines' was reported as 600. to_int was not, so it tested '1,400' with str.isdigit(), got False, fell through to the number words and returned None. _rederive_quoted builds its token list from it, so the list collapsed to empty and the gate reported that the quoted string 'carries no numeral at all' about a string that reads 1,400. No figure of four digits or more could take the honest quoted route. Slide 4's 1,400 hit it this run and was routed through computed_by instead. A gate that refuses the honest route teaches a run that the shortcut passes.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

THE RECORD. The worklist was cleared in full, sixteen of sixteen re-verified against primary sources, and staleness is now zero due. Two corrections were forced by the primary record. Five items admitted, and one held: the Waymo Houston opening has no beat for AI in the field and no decider type for a company, so it sits in the seed with the real reason written down rather than being filed under a lane that does not fit it. THE FINDING THAT NEEDS A HUMAN. Thirty nine of the fifty eight county pages tell a reader the county is outside every metropolitan area, and all thirty nine are inside one. site_build prints that sentence unconditionally instead of only when places.metro_of returns nothing. Nine gates ran green over it. scripts/site/site_build.py is human owned, so this run may not fix it. The proposal is in the run record. THE DECK, AND THE EXPENSIVE PART OF THIS RUN. It was scored ten times. The first four ended at 7.27 and it shipped. CI then went red on three site gates, all three reading slide one, and repairing them changed copy the panel had already judged. A changed frame makes the score stale, which gate_status reads as a red row by design, so the deck went back to the panel. It went back four more times and every round found something. It ships at 7.42, unanimous, no hard fail. TWO PANELS FAILED IT OUTRIGHT AND BOTH HARD FAILS WERE THE SAME DEFECT. The composition chose a word and the fact was fitted to it afterwards. The cover said "No column for it" over a byline of a dateline and a mileage figure, neither of which supports an absence, and this run's own rejected list says in writing that the TxDOT crash query never rendered and an absence cannot be asserted from a page that did not render. It now asks instead. Slide 7 said "DPS publishes first responder interaction plans" where its cited claim says the page takes them, because an acceptance item in the plan had written the verb PUBLISH into it. Both the frame and the acceptance item are fixed, and an acceptance item may no longer choose a verb. Every carousel gate stayed green through both, because a gate can check that a cited claim id resolves and cannot check whether the sentence above it says what the claim says. THE WORST PROCESS ERROR WAS MINE AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH READING. build_slides.py was run with its output suppressed and its exit code unread. Its own footer check REFUSED the build, correctly, naming a byline seventy two pixels too wide, and exited into a suppressed stream. The previous build's HTML was still on disk, so the renderer rendered it, machine QA passed it, eleven carousel gates passed it, and three scoring judges graded a deck that had never been built. One judge caught it by comparing the pixels against the plan and said so in its first paragraph. The house rule says run a GATE by exit code. The gap is that the BUILDER is not a gate and nobody had said to read its code too. WHAT IS CARRIED RATHER THAN FIXED. Slide 8's declared focal, a milled band of lit groove lips, does not exist in the render. The relief ran inside the letterforms instead of milling the band around them, so the type reads raised where the plan wanted it cut. Six craft readings across six panels ruled it a failed technique rather than an unfinished frame, and four of them said in writing that a judge ruling the other way would be reasonable. The artwork ledger now records the drawing that actually shipped rather than the one that was planned, which is the one thing that file exists to make impossible and had already failed once. SEVENTEEN PROPOSALS ARE FILED IN THE RUN RECORD, all outside the record's own lane. The one worth reading first is a gate that would diff the shipped render's own copy.json against the storyboard's declared hooks, deks and bylines. It is the tenth panel's own one sentence fix and it would have caught the build that never ran.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
